candidates.prompt_text: Which sport do you like to play or watch most? Please describe it and say why you like it.
suggested_ideas: where you usually play or watch it
what you do in the sport
one simple reason you like it

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker names one sport and gives a short personal description with a simple reason for liking it.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear sport choice; at least one detail about playing or watching; one basic reason such as fun, healthy, exciting, or easy to join.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any common or less common sport is acceptable. The student may talk about playing, watching, or both. Short simple answers are acceptable if they stay on the topic.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking mainly about school subjects, food, a famous person without mentioning the sport choice, or a general talk about exercise with no sport named.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: For pronunciation, listen for clear individual words, especially the sport name and common simple sentences. Minor grammar errors are fine if words are understandable. A very short but clear response can still be acceptable.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not naming a sport clearly; giving only one word with no support; mispronouncing key words so the sport is hard to identify; going off topic to talk about unrelated hobbies.

candidates.prompt_text: Do you prefer team sports or individual sports? Give an example and explain your choice.
suggested_ideas: say team sports or individual sports
give one example such as football, badminton, running, or swimming
say one or two reasons for your choice

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker chooses between team sports and individual sports, gives one example, and explains the choice in simple language.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear preference; one example sport; one or two easy reasons such as working with others, being independent, being active, or feeling relaxed.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Either option is acceptable. The student may use a familiar sport from school or daily life. Simple comparison language is enough.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking only about a favorite athlete, discussing rules of many sports without making a choice, or speaking about video games or music instead of sports.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Focus on intelligibility of short connected speech. Check whether key contrast words like team, individual, prefer, because, and the sport example are pronounced clearly enough to understand.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Not making a clear choice; giving an example that does not match the chosen type; repeating the same idea without explanation; unclear pronunciation of the main preference words.

candidates.prompt_text: If you can choose one sport for your free time this week, what will you choose? Say what you need and why it is a good choice for you.
suggested_ideas: say simple things you need, for example a ball, a racket, or open space
say why it is good for your free time this week

evaluation_guide.expected_content: The speaker chooses one sport for the near future, mentions simple things needed for it, and gives a personal reason.
evaluation_guide.key_points: A clear sport choice; one or two basic items or conditions needed; a simple reason such as fun, healthy, relaxing, or suitable for free time.
evaluation_guide.acceptable_responses: Any accessible sport is acceptable, including walking, running, football, badminton, basketball, or skipping rope. Students may answer with simple future meaning even if grammar is not perfect.
evaluation_guide.off_topic_examples: Talking about a full weekly schedule without choosing a sport, discussing shopping plans in detail, or describing a holiday activity unrelated to sports.
evaluation_guide.scoring_hints: Judge pronunciation by how clearly the student says the chosen sport, needed items, and short reason. Simple words said clearly should score better than longer unclear sentences.
evaluation_guide.common_mistakes: Forgetting to mention what is needed; choosing an activity that is not clearly a sport; listing many objects without a reason; pronunciation that makes key nouns hard to understand.
